headline: High: dexter’s broad egress and financial-data access can leak or misroute sensitive outputs into Rasa’s chat channels; prompt-injection and workflow-cascade risks are otherwise moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter can write to .dexter/scratchpad/ and uses autonomous execution with broad network egress, while rasa ingests external chat inputs via Slack/Messenger/Twilio-style channels. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content can reach dexter or be reinterpreted by rasa, though no shared channel is documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF dexter reads content from .dexter/scratchpad/ as instructions
IF rasa forwards untrusted channel text into downstream automation
IF the two agents are connected through a shared chat or file bridge
mitigations: Disable any automatic ingestion of scratchpad contents
Insert a human review step before either agent acts on external text
Restrict rasa to a single trusted channel for testing
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
requires-engineering: isolate the agents with separate workspaces and no shared queue

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API keys, while rasa exposes chat integrations that can carry user text and voice. If dexter’s outputs or context are routed into rasa, sensitive data can be exfiltrated or echoed to third-party messaging services. The pairwise path is not directly documented, so confidence is moderate, but the blast radius is clearly sensitive.
conditions: IF dexter outputs financial data into any shared channel
IF rasa relays that content to Slack, Twilio, or another external connector
IF both agents are given the same sensitive workspace or transcript
mitigations: Remove sensitive data from shared transcripts
Turn off external chat connectors during evaluation
Use separate credentials for each agent
Redact financial fields before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while rasa does not support multiple instances and is oriented around chat integrations. Overlap is limited because rasa shows no filesystem write surface, but if both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or shared state, conflicts can corrupt outputs. The interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or transcript store
IF an orchestrator launches multiple dexter instances against shared state
IF rasa is configured to mutate shared conversation artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run only one writer per shared resource
Snapshot shared files before each run
Lock mutable artifacts during handoff
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter can generate research outputs from external APIs, and rasa’s dialogue-understanding subagent can consume text and produce responses. If rasa treats dexter’s output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into user-facing answers or actions. No direct evidence shows this exact pipeline, so uncertainty keeps it at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF rasa uses dexter-generated text as source material
IF no verification step checks dexter’s claims before response generation
IF downstream users rely on rasa’s answers for decisions
mitigations: Require citation checks before reuse
Add a confidence threshold for handoff
Route dexter outputs to a review queue
Log source provenance with each claim
requires-engineering: implement fact-validation against primary sources

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data and requests multiple API keys, while rasa routes text and voice through third-party messaging and telephony connectors. If regulated financial or personal data is sent through those connectors, compliance breach risk is material. The profiles do not document residency or DPA controls, so uncertainty escalates rather than lowers severity.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is sent through rasa connectors
IF voice or chat transcripts contain personal data
IF no DPA, retention, or residency controls are configured
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through external connectors
Minimize retained transcripts
Use test data only for integration checks
Review connector vendor terms before deployment
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
